chunks: And it is narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man asks me to bear testimony, and I recognize my handwriting and my seal, but I do not remember anything else, whether little or much.
So he عليه السلام said: “If your companion is trustworthy, and you have a trustworthy man with you, then testify for him.”

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةِ: legal testimony or witness-bearing in a formal matter
key_terms.ثِقَةً: trustworthy, reliable in character and report
key_terms.خَاتَمِي: my seal, used as a mark of authentication
key_terms.خَطِّي: my handwriting, serving as identifying written evidence

ai.seo_question: Can a person testify if he recognizes his handwriting and seal but does not remember the details?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal question regarding testimony when a person recognizes his own handwriting and seal but does not recall the remaining details. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permits giving testimony when the person involved is trustworthy and another trustworthy man is present, indicating the role of reliability in judicial testimony.
